bobbin.value: M class aluminum bobbin, case type MF; rotary hook, horizontal axis (manual wording)

motor.value: Brushless DC with up and down needle positioning and tie-off stitch; 300 W peak; 105 to 120 VAC, 47 to 63 Hz (US and Canada), 100 to 250 VAC (rest of world)

frame.value: No frame; sit-down machine with a table that has height-adjustable folding legs and weighs nearly 50 lb; 18 x 30 in table extensions sold separately; base table size and height range not published by the maker

conflicts: Hook: the Handi Quilter user manual v3.3 (library-hosted copy) says 'Rotary, Horizontal axis', while our earlier spec read 'rotary vertical hook'; the spec now follows the manual.
Voltage: the manual v3.3 gives 105 to 120 VAC for the US and Canada and 100 to 250 VAC for the rest of the world, while our earlier spec said 90 to 264 VAC; the spec now follows the manual.
Motor: the manual confirms a brushless DC motor with tie-off and 300 W peak; the earlier voltage range in the motor line did not match either manual line and has been replaced.
Speed: the manual v3.3 and the dealer-hosted v3.1 copy both give 1500 spm maximum, while the Rocky Mountain Sewing dealer page says up to 1,800 spm; the page uses the manual figure.
Stitch regulation: the manual lists TruStitch as an optional accessory, while the Rocky Mountain Sewing dealer page says TruStitch is included with its package; check the quote line by line.

Throat: the maker prints 'Throat Dimensions 8.25 x 16 in' and calls it a '16-inch sit-down longarm' without saying needle to body; 16 in is the maker's wording, not a measured needle-to-body figure, and in our tiering a 16 in head sits in the mid-arm band.

Status: 'discontinued' appears on a dealer page (Rocky Mountain Sewing); Handi Quilter carries no machine page, only a parts tag archive, and a maker support article refers to the 'secondary used-machine market'.

Price: the $6,495 dealer-level figure equals the Handi Quilter list price shown for the Moxie ST, and the maker publishes no price for the Sweet Sixteen itself, so treat it as an unconfirmed dealer figure and read it as a band, not a quote.
Table: the manual gives no base table size or height range; 36 x 30 in and 26 to 42 in come from dealer copy, and dealers disagree on the range (26 to 42 in against 27 to 40 in).
Weight and size: the maker publishes no machine weight and no head dimensions; the 66.14 lb figure on the maker's lift table page is packaging for that accessory only.

editorial.verdict: A discontinued 16 in sit-down quilter with a table and optional regulation, for a buyer who wants more throat than a domestic without a frame.
editorial.whoFor: A quilter who wants more reach than a domestic machine without giving a room to a frame, and who is happy to adjust tension and move fabric by hand on a table.
editorial.skipIf: You want stitch regulation included, you quilt king size tops often (owners report the weight of heavy quilts on the table), or you want a model Handi Quilter still lists as a machine.
editorial.keySpec: 8.25 x 16 in throat (maker wording) · 1500 spm · sit-down table · regulation optional
realCost: Stitch regulation: TruStitch is an optional accessory per the manual; one dealer says it is included, so confirm it in the quote
Lift table with built-in InSight regulation: $2,645.00 on the Handi Quilter accessory page, for TruStitch-compatible machines on firmware 3.18 or higher
Table extensions: 18 x 30 in, sold separately per the manual
Consumables: 134 (135x7) needles in 12/80 to 20/125 and M class bobbins
strengths: Owners report the sit-down table suits quilters who prefer moving the fabric by hand, and several say they quilt twin and larger sizes on it with a hanging system for the biggest
Owners of a decade or more report few or no reliability problems, with some calling it a workhorse, though others describe it as persnickety
The retailer page shows a 4.76 rating across 17 reviews at Sewing Machines Plus, which skews positive as seller-collected feedback
weaknesses: Owners report that heavy quilts drag on the table and are hard to support, and one shop worker reports timing knocked out by very heavy seams
Owners report tension taking time to set, including trouble after oiling, though others say it is easy with fine thread
Owners report missing promotional feet and note the sit-down has no presser foot or feed dogs, which is its own trade-off for ruler and edge work

faqs.q: Is the Handi Quilter Sweet Sixteen discontinued?
faqs.a: A dealer page (Rocky Mountain Sewing) says so. Handi Quilter's own wording is that the machine is on the secondary used-machine market, and its site carries no machine page for it, only parts.

faqs.q: How big is the Sweet Sixteen throat?
faqs.a: The maker prints throat dimensions of 8.25 x 16 in (245 x 610 mm) and calls it a 16-inch sit-down longarm. It does not say needle to body.

faqs.q: Is the Sweet Sixteen a long-arm?
faqs.a: The maker calls it a sit-down longarm. In our tiering a 16 in head sits in the mid-arm band, so treat the maker's term as marketing wording rather than a throat class.

faqs.q: How fast does the Sweet Sixteen sew?
faqs.a: The manual lists 1500 spm maximum, in both the v3.3 and v3.1 copies. One dealer page says up to 1,800 spm; this page uses the manual figure.

faqs.q: Does the Sweet Sixteen have a stitch regulator?
faqs.a: Not built in. The manual lists TruStitch as an optional accessory, and Handi Quilter sells a lift table with built-in InSight regulation for compatible machines. One dealer says TruStitch is included with its package.
The manual gives 105 to 120 VAC at 47 to 63 Hz for the US and Canada, with a brushless DC motor at 300 W peak.

faqs.q: What needle and bobbin does the Sweet Sixteen use?
faqs.a: The manual lists 134 (135x7) needles in sizes 12/80 to 20/125 and an M class aluminum bobbin with a type MF case.

faqs.q: How much does a Sweet Sixteen weigh?
faqs.a: Handi Quilter does not publish the machine weight. The manual says the table weighs nearly 50 lb.
The maker's warranty page lists 90 days, 10 years on the casting, 5 years mechanical and 5 years electrical, with registration required. The text is not model-specific.
Handi Quilter staff comments name the Moxie ST and Amara ST as the stationary machines still offered. The maker does not call either a direct replacement.
